findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion and regression case covering the newly HEAD-strengthened WRITE gate (event_prepare._ensure_initialized): a `.git`-present-but-HEAD-unresolvable store must reject writes, and an empty-initialized store must still accept them.
evidence: Plan: 'The shared predicate unifies the read guard with the `.git`-presence base of event_prepare._ensure_initialized and strengthens both with HEAD resolution.'
Plan Files lists event_prepare.py as changed but only tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py for coverage
Code: event_prepare._ensure_initialized currently checks only `not os.path.exists(os.path.join(tracker, '.git'))` (src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py:101)
All 5 ACs are phrased as 'reads as ...' / 'still READS'
findings.finding: The plan deliberately strengthens the WRITE gate (event_prepare._ensure_initialized) from a bare `.git`-presence check to also require a resolvable HEAD ('strengthens both with HEAD resolution'), which changes write-path behavior — a store with `.git` present but HEAD unresolvable that previously passed the write init check will now be rejected — yet every acceptance criterion and the named regression file (test_reads_uninitialized_store.py) exercise only READ behavior, leaving the changed write-gate behavior unverified.
findings.location: Fix plan -> 'The read/write init gates, precisely' + Acceptance criteria + Files (event_prepare.py)
scenarios: A mid-clone or partially-fetched store where `.git` exists but HEAD is not yet resolvable now fails a write with 'not initialized' where it previously did not

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how store_is_usable treats git rev-parse subprocess failures (missing binary, non-zero exit, hang): map all non-resolvable outcomes to 'not usable' (store_uninitialized) and state a timeout so a locked/hung .git cannot block the read path.
evidence: Predicate: 'isdir AND .git present AND git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD resolves'
The production incident originated on a store dir that is itself an xfs MOUNT POINT (/dev/nvme1n1); a mid-clone .git can hold a lock
The existing reducer path only catches 'except OSError: return results' — a subprocess raising a different exception or hanging is unaddressed
findings.finding: The new store_is_usable predicate shells out to `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, a new subprocess failure point on the read path, but the plan does not specify how subprocess-level failures (git binary missing, a hung/locked .git mid-clone, timeout) are handled — only the clean non-zero-exit 'HEAD does not resolve' case.
scenarios: git binary unavailable in the MCP runtime -> FileNotFoundError propagates as an unhandled error instead of a clean store_uninitialized
A mid-clone .git with a lock causes git rev-parse to hang -> read blocks with no timeout
findings.suggested_fix: State that store_is_usable runs git rev-parse with a bounded timeout and treats ANY failure (non-zero exit, timeout, subprocess exception) as 'not a usable store', returning False rather than propagating.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the deliberate three-gate asymmetry (reads: .git+HEAD, no .env-id; writes: +.env-id) in a durable location (module docstring on store_usability.py, an ADR, or AGENTS.md) so it survives beyond this ticket.
evidence: 'There are THREE init-related gates and they are deliberately NOT all identical'
'Reads DELIBERATELY do NOT adopt the .env-id predicate' — a non-obvious invariant that AC4 protects but no durable doc records
The plan itself notes a related inconsistency already filed (ab61-f3e8-6ee6-4905) showing these gates drift
findings.finding: The plan establishes a deliberate three-gate model (reads require .git+HEAD but NOT .env-id; writes require .env-id; low-level append checks .git-presence) with subtle rationale, but does not capture this decision in an ADR/AGENTS.md/design-doc so a future maintainer won't 'unify' the gates and reintroduce the bug.
findings.location: Fix plan -> 'The read/write init gates, precisely'
scenarios: A future refactor tries to make reads and writes share the .env-id predicate for 'consistency' and breaks just-cloned-store reads
findings.suggested_fix: Add a module-level docstring to store_usability.py stating why reads intentionally omit .env-id while writes require it, and reference the AC4 regression that guards it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile store_is_usable with the existing predicates before adding a new leaf: reuse/reference sync._ok / init._git_ok for the `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` check and gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir for worktree-aware `.git` detection (or state explicitly why a stdlib-only leaf cannot depend on them, e.g. the import-SCC constraint, and why the `.git`-as-file case is safe to ignore).
evidence: Plan Design: 'Factor a SHARED usability predicate into a new stdlib-only leaf src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py::store_is_usable(tracker) = isdir AND .git present AND git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD resolves.'
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:85 `def _ok(tracker, *args) -> bool: return _git(tracker, *args).returncode == 0` — an existing HEAD-resolution primitive.
src/rebar/_commands/init.py:83 `def _git_ok(cwd, *args) -> bool: return _git(cwd, *args).returncode == 0` — a second existing copy of the same predicate.

src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:72 `_resolve_tracker_git_dir(tracker)` already resolves `.git` including the `.git`-as-FILE (gitdir pointer / linked-worktree) case, which the plan's bare os.path.exists(tracker/.git) presence check does not handle.

A prior plan-review finding is cached raising this same point: '.rebar/cache/plan-review/aefe-614a-2631-4117/…json: Reference the existing HEAD-resolution predicates (sync._ok / init._git_ok) and the worktree-aware .git resolution (gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_di…'
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new store_usability.store_is_usable() that re-implements HEAD-resolution (git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD == returncode 0) and .git-presence detection that already exist in the codebase (sync._ok, init._git_ok, and the worktree-aware gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir), without referencing or reconciling with them.
scenarios: The tracker is a linked git worktree where `.git` is a file (gitdir: pointer) rather than a directory: the plan's os.path.exists(tracker/.git) presence check passes but a naive rev-parse from tracker could still misbehave, whereas gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir already models this case.
A future maintainer must now keep THREE HEAD-resolution predicates (sync._ok, init._git_ok, store_usability) in sync.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Design section, add a subsection reconciling the new predicate with the three existing helpers: cite sync._ok/init._git_ok as the prior art for the HEAD check and gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir for `.git` resolution, and justify duplication only via the concrete import-SCC constraint (stdlib-only leaf, no rebar back-edges); if the `.git`-as-file worktree case is in scope, delegate detection to _resolve_tracker_git_dir's logic rather than a bare os.path.exists.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the non-audit consumers of the 7 affected read entry points (rebar._reads importers in _lib_reads.py, llm/*, _commands/close_autoresume.py; rebar.list_tickets callers in _mcp_reads.py, llm/code_review/*, review_bot/artifact_emit.py, audit/read.py) and confirm none relied on []-for-present-but-broken-store, rather than backing the 'no caller depends' claim with only the single store_uninitialized-catching audit consumer.
evidence: Plan quote: 'The ONLY consumer of the store_uninitialized code is rebar.audit.server._audited_tickets ... No caller depends on the old []-for-broken-store behaviour.'

search 'from rebar import _reads' -> src/rebar/_lib_reads.py, src/rebar/llm/completion.py, enrich.py, operations.py, plan_review/*, workflow/*, code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py, overlap/digest_sidecar.py, src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py (all outside src/rebar/_store/ and src/rebar/audit/).
search 'rebar.list_tickets' -> src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:311, src/rebar/llm/code_review/{sidecar,finalize,fp_ledger}.py, src/rebar/review_bot/artifact_emit.py, src/rebar/audit/read.py:163.

Mitigating: CHANGELOG.md:33-46 shows the ABSENT-store store_uninitialized raise already shipped, so consumers tolerate the raise; only the present-but-broken/mid-clone case is newly affected. This narrows but does not close the gap.
The same gap was raised in a prior round (.rebar/cache/plan-review/aefe-614a-2631-4117) and the rev2 gate text still lists only the audit consumer.
findings.finding: The 'Caller-dependency gate' asserts 'No caller depends on the old []-for-broken-store behaviour' but enumerates only the single store_uninitialized-catching consumer (rebar.audit.server._audited_tickets), while many other modules OUTSIDE the artifact dir consume the affected read entry points and see their behavior change for a present-but-broken / mid-clone store (now raises instead of []).
scenarios: A driving-agent orchestration path (e.g. llm/workflow or plan_review) that today silently sees [] against a mid-clone store now receives a RebarError it does not catch, aborting the run instead of retrying.
src/rebar/audit/read.py:163 or review_bot/artifact_emit.py enumerating code_review artifacts against a repo whose store is mid-clone begins raising where it previously degraded to [].
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the Caller-dependency gate to list the read consumers outside src/rebar/_store and src/rebar/audit, note that the ABSENT-store raise already shipped (CHANGELOG.md:33-46) so they already tolerate store_uninitialized, and state explicitly for each cohort (or as a class) that none branched on []-for-broken-store; call out any that degrade on [] (e.g. audit/read.py, review_bot/artifact_emit.py) and confirm the new mid-clone/broken raise is acceptable there.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the per-read cost of the unconditional `git rev-parse HEAD` on the _tracker chokepoint (7 entry points) and either justify it as negligible or reuse the existing throttle/local-read-context so hot read loops do not spawn an extra git process per read.
evidence: Plan: 'Read predicate: `.git` present AND `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves' called from the read chokepoint on every read
Plan Blast radius: '`_reads._tracker` funnels 7 read entry points'

Code: reads.ensure_fresh guards per-read git cost with a /tmp throttle marker (<=1/min) and _LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT early-return (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:235-268); store_is_usable has no equivalent
findings.finding: The shared store_is_usable predicate adds an unconditional `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` subprocess to `_reads._tracker()`, which the plan itself notes funnels 7 read entry points; unlike the adjacent freshness path (ensure_fresh) it has no throttle marker, no cache, and no _LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT bypass, so every read now spawns an extra git process on a hot chokepoint with no stated cost consideration.
scenarios: High-frequency scripted read/transform loops (the same loops cited in bug slim-fetch-ledge) now pay one extra git subprocess per read
Large-batch orchestrator reads calling list_tickets/ready repeatedly

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider reusing the existing worktree-aware gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir (and any existing HEAD-resolution helper) inside store_is_usable rather than a fresh os.path.exists(.git) check, so the usability predicate matches the store's real (possibly worktree) `.git` layout — or state why the simpler os.path.exists check is sufficient.
evidence: Plan: predicate '= isdir AND `.git` present AND `git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD` resolves', inheriting event_prepare's os.path.exists(.git)
Code: gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir(tracker) already handles both `.git`-as-file (worktree, 'gitdir: ' redirect) and `.git`-as-dir (src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:72-83)
findings.finding: The design introduces a new leaf that reimplements `.git` detection via os.path.exists, while the codebase already has gitutil._resolve_tracker_git_dir which robustly resolves the worktree `.git`-FILE (gitdir: redirection) case that trackers commonly use; the plan does not consider reusing it, risking a subtly weaker `.git` check than the existing resolver.
scenarios: Tracker deployed as a git worktree (the common MCP deployment shape) where `.git` is a file pointing at the real gitdir
